means: Two players against one defender. The defender can't guard both, so somebody is always open.
A play the coach draws up during a timeout. Coaches call them ATO plays.
A screen set behind a defender, on the side away from the ball, so a teammate can cut to the basket.
When your defender stands between you and the ball, run behind them, straight to the basket.
Passing the ball quickly from player to player. The ball moves faster than any defender can run.
The line at the end of the court, under the basket. A baseline cut or drive runs right along it.
Passing the ball in from behind the baseline, under the basket you're shooting at. Coaches call it BLOB.
A tall player who usually plays close to the basket, setting screens and grabbing rebounds.
A triangle play: when the top player is guarded, a teammate flashes to the high post, and the top player cuts behind their defender.
A pass that bounces once on the floor on the way to your teammate. It's hard for a tall defender to reach.
An inbound setup with four players in a square: two by the basket and two at the free-throw line.
After a shot, step in front of the player you guard with your back to them, so you get to the rebound first.
A defense where four players guard a box near the basket and one chases the best shooter everywhere.
Run at a player who just caught the ball, then take short steps with your hands up to bother the shot.
An offense that keeps going around and around: when the play ends, everyone is set up to run it again.
The spot where the baseline meets the sideline. A shot from there is the shortest three-pointer on the court.
Bouncing the ball low across your body from one hand to the other, so you can change direction fast.
Running tight around a screen and into the middle, when your defender is chasing right behind you.
Running quickly to a new spot, often toward the basket, to get open for a pass.
Trying to stop the other team from scoring. Team defense means all five players help each other.
Standing in the passing lane, between your player and the ball, so they can't catch a pass.
Two teammates standing side by side to make one big screen.
A screen set by a player who runs down toward the baseline, so a teammate down low can come up and get open.
Bouncing the ball with one hand while you move. You have to dribble to go anywhere with the ball.
Dribbling toward a teammate and handing them the ball as they run past you.
A practice activity you repeat again and again to get better at one skill.
Dribbling hard toward the basket to score or to make the defense help.
Drive toward the basket to pull defenders in, then pass out to an open shooter.
The corner where the free-throw line meets the side of the paint. In the triangle, a player there is at the pinch post.
A play where a shooter runs between two teammates, and they step together behind them like elevator doors closing.
A pass to a teammate in the post, close to the basket.
Pretending to do one thing, like shoot, so your defender jumps, then doing something else.
Racing up the court after getting the ball, before the defense can get back.
All five players stand outside the 3-point line, leaving the middle open for cuts and drives.
An offense that repeats: a pass across the top, a flex cut along the baseline, then a down screen.
A cut from the corner along the baseline, off a screen from the teammate on the block.
The screen for a flex cut, set by the player on the block.
A play where a shooter starts under the basket and picks which way to run out, with screens waiting on both sides.
How you move your feet: stepping, stopping and turning, all without traveling.
The basic skills every player needs: catching, dribbling, passing, shooting and playing defense.
The open spaces between zone defenders. Stand in a gap and two defenders have to decide who guards you.
Moving to a spot where a teammate can pass you the ball without a defender in the way.
A play where one player drives along the baseline while a teammate gets screened into the corner for a three.
Handing the ball to a teammate as they run close past you, instead of passing it.
When the screener's defender jumps out in front of the dribbler to slow them down, then runs back to their own player.
Being ready to step over and stop a player who gets past your teammate.
Slowing down for a moment like you're about to stop, then speeding up past your defender.
The area around the free-throw line, at the top of the paint.
A setup with two players at the elbows, like the two horns of a bull, and two in the corners.
Passing the ball onto the court from out of bounds.
A quick, short step at your defender with one foot, keeping the other foot still, to see how they react.
A shot you take while jumping straight up, usually from farther away than a layup.
Stopping with both feet landing at the same time, so you're balanced and haven't traveled.
A shot from right next to the basket, often bounced in off the backboard.
An inbound setup where everyone lines up one behind the other, like train cars, then breaks out.
In the triangle, the straight line from the ball through the post player to the hoop. On that line, the post's defender is stuck behind them.
Everything you do when you don't have the ball, like cutting, screening and getting open.
One player with the ball against one defender.
Throwing the ball to a teammate.
The path the ball would take on a pass. Put a hand in it, and the pass hits your hand instead.
Like the pick and roll, but the screener steps out for a shot instead of rolling to the basket.
A teammate sets a screen for the dribbler, then turns and rolls to the basket.
The spots players stand in to start a play, and the jobs that go with each spot.
The area near the basket, just outside the paint. To post up, stand there with your defender on your back and call for the ball.
Watching what the defenders do, then picking the move that beats them.
Grabbing the ball after a missed shot.
Running back to your own player after helping a teammate.
Sliding over to cover for a teammate who left their player, like when two teammates trap the ball.
Standing still like a wall so a teammate's defender bumps into you. Also called a pick.
When the player who just set a screen gets a screen from another teammate, and pops open.
Throwing the ball at the basket to score.
A player who is great at making shots, especially from far away. Defenses work hard to stop them.
Lifting the ball like you're about to shoot, but keeping it, so your defender jumps.
Passing the ball in from the side of the court. Coaches call it SLOB.
Moving sideways on defense with quick steps, without crossing your feet, so you stay in front of your player.
Standing far enough apart that one defender can't guard two players at once.
A pick and roll with a twist: a third player sets a back screen on the screener's defender. It's named after Spain's national team.
An inbound setup where players line up side by side at the free-throw line, then split apart.
Two screens in a row, one after the other, for the same teammate.
The ready position on defense: knees bent, feet wide, hands out.
Getting in front of the dribbler on a fast break, so they have to slow down and can't get a layup.
When two defenders trade the players they guard, usually because of a screen.
Calling out to your teammates, like “Switch!” or “Ball!”, so everyone knows what's happening.
Working together. A good pass helps the team as much as a good shot.
A shot from behind the 3-point line. It counts for 3 points instead of 2.
Running back on defense the moment the other team gets the ball, faster than the ball.
Two defenders guarding the player with the ball at the same time, so it's hard to dribble or pass.
Taking steps while holding the ball without dribbling. It's against the rules, and the other team gets the ball.
An offense where three players make a triangle on one side of the court and the other two wait on the other side.
A defense where two players chase the two best shooters and the other three guard a triangle by the basket.
Holding the ball low by your hip, facing the hoop, ready to shoot, pass or dribble.
Two teammates working together to beat their two defenders, like a pick and roll or a handoff.
Easy moves at the start of practice to get your body ready to play.
The weak side is the side away from the ball. A flash is a quick cut toward the ball, often to the high post.
A cut straight up from the block to the top, past a screen, like pulling up a zipper.
A defense where each player guards an area instead of one player. Zone offense is how you beat it.
